authority: observer-centered angular navigation and provenance metadata only; no fate, personality, readiness, identity, governance, Treasury, or capability authority
purpose: Define how a geocentric Tempus portal can preserve twelve equal tropical zodiac sectors, actual IAU constellation regions, and dodecahedral face navigation without falsely claiming that regular dodecahedron faces are literal equal ecliptic sky patches.

observer_posture.default_observer: Earth geocenter for global Tempus sky context
observer_posture.law: A Viewpoint May Be Central to Experience Without Being Central to Cosmology.

ecliptic_direction_math.note: Reference frame and epoch/of-date rule must be declared before lambda/beta values are compared across time.

tropical_zodiac.anchor: 0 degrees Aries = tropical/equinox reference direction in the selected of-date convention
tropical_zodiac.relation_to_72_sector_registry: each 30-degree sign contains six neutral 5-degree sectors

iau_constellation_layer.lookup_rule: Resolve a sky direction against official IAU constellation boundaries in an appropriate celestial coordinate frame; do not infer the constellation from tropical sign index.
iau_constellation_layer.important_boundary: Tropical zodiac sign, IAU constellation, and physical stellar neighborhood are three different data layers.

dodecahedral_portal_geometry.face_normals: the twelve regular-dodecahedron face normals form the twelve vertices of the dual regular icosahedron
dodecahedral_portal_geometry.proof_posture: The twelve dual-icosahedron vertices are not coplanar. A rigid rotation preserves coplanarity, so no orientation can place all twelve face normals onto the one ecliptic great circle as twelve 30-degree directions.
dodecahedral_portal_geometry.consequence: A dodecahedral face may index or frame a zodiac portal, but face normal and zodiac-center direction are distinct coordinates.
dodecahedral_portal_geometry.candidate_law: Face Index and Sky Direction Are Different Coordinates.

portal_modes.description: Twelve dodecahedral faces act as stable UI houses. Each face is assigned one tropical sign index, but the physical face normal is not presented as that sign's true sky bearing.
When a face/sign is selected, rotate the dodecahedral UI so the selected face normal aligns with the actual target direction, e.g. sign center or selected body direction.
portal_modes.other_faces: become surrounding navigation geometry only and must not simultaneously be claimed as the other eleven zodiac bearings
portal_modes.scientific_posture: safe if clearly shown as camera/UI rotation
portal_modes.preferred_for: looking outward through one star house

portal_modes.description: Use actual IAU boundary and star-catalog data in the viewport while retaining the dodecahedron only as frame/chrome.

motion_semantics.sun: geocentric apparent solar longitude moves through the tropical sectors over the year
motion_semantics.moon: geocentric lunar longitude moves faster and independently; latitude is retained separately
motion_semantics.planets: geocentric apparent longitudes may show direct/stationary/retrograde apparent motion depending on observer-relative geometry
motion_semantics.stars: on human timescales the background is comparatively slow, but precession/proper motion and epoch matter for long-term precision
motion_semantics.signs: tropical signs remain an equinox-anchored angular partition rather than star groups moving inside literal pentagonal faces

geocentric_heliocentric_bridge.physical_scene: Use heliocentric/barycentric ephemeris state vectors for the solar-system model.
geocentric_heliocentric_bridge.lived_sky: Transform/request observer-centered apparent coordinates for what an Earth observer sees.
geocentric_heliocentric_bridge.sun_example: In a common geometric ecliptic frame, geocentric Sun direction is opposite Earth's heliocentric position vector; production apparent longitude uses full ephemeris corrections.
geocentric_heliocentric_bridge.law: Geocentric Perspective Is an Observer Frame, Not a Cosmological Claim.
